content.rendered: Ha! And my wife says I’m quick!

Lmao. That was quick.

BAHAHAHAHAHAHAHAHAHAHAHA

THAT IS FUCKING HILARIOUS LOOOOOOL

In all seriousness, everyone working in U.S. Bank’s Actuarial, Underwriting & Product department who gave this the green light should be fired. Incredibly embarrassing to have to discontinue a product <1 year because you couldn’t do……math.

I mean seriously, U.S. Bank could’ve just paid for a sponsored post on DOC asking if this was a good idea and we would’ve told them NO for free!
Glad I skipped the inevitable nerf, and that was with expecting it to stick around for 2-3 years.

Just called usbank to pc a cash plus or a usbank go to smartly, and was told that smartly card is no longer an option for product changes. Also not able to apply in branch either, only online currently. They were unaware if card is being discontinued but said applications were suspended in branch.

Question is, is it still worth it to apply now in hope that it will just be discontinued but not killed off entirely?

If they are really doing as bad as thought to be with this card, I can’t imagine they’ll just let people ride it along for much longer.
Someone got fired.

Go figure. 2.5% cards can’t even survive.

https://www.doctorofcredit.com/usaa-to-discontinue-limitless-2-5-cashback-card-existing-cardholders-to-be-converted/
Lot of people are going to be angry as they played games to move 100k+ only to her nerfed under a year. Grandfathering cards is a toss.
Watch them change it to 1.5% like their discontinued Cash 365 Amex.
Isn’t there a Federal law (or regulation) which prohibits CC companies from product changing/cancelling cards under a year old?
Yup. This is going to be a major blow to their reputation.
Pretty high chance they probably just nerf it to 1.5 – 2% everywhere only. Otherwise, they might do forced PC after a couple of years or something like that.

I would hope that US Bank would not want a run on the bank if they totally canceled existing cardholders. Maybe they would lower the percentage down to 3.5% or 3%, and see what kind of exodus, if any, occurs? Or, maybe place a monthly spending cap on existing cardholders to earn the 4%? [Cliffhanger].
5.25 is capped at 2.5k per quarter and limited to certain categories, albeit a great one like online but still…. vs 4% catch all no cap.

You are forgetting thats only for one category that is chosen and its not every possible MCC. Plus, you can only swap the category once a month and there is the quarterly cap. Smartly is all purchases.

Not worth it imo. If it’s costing U.S. Bank this much money they won’t be grandfathering and continuing to herodge losses for X period of time.

My bet would be is they’ll send out cancelation/forced PC notices and offer all cardholders an inconvenience cash bonus/credit of like $500.

Because you have to remember people moved 6 figures in assets to qualify for this and to pull a bait & switch like this is EXTREMELY uncool.

It’s over Johnny, It’s Over !
2025 cutting spree is on!

U.S. Bank had plenty of funds on hand before they started this card… And I’m sure they will be just fine without it and the $100K cronies who signed up.

If I was a betting person, I’d say no grandfathering will occur and you can your pick of Cash+ or others by XX date, or close by XX.
Really debating if going 5/24 is gnna be worth it now. The dced USBAR hasn’t been nerfed yet right?

Ah I think you’re assuming that we use for booking travel and take advantage of the bonus (reasonable), which would make the math as 1.5*1.75*1.2 = 3.15.

That said, is the BofA travel center appropriate priced? Chase loves selling tickets with inflated prices that wipe out any discount you get upfront.

Wonder how long they’ll be without a premium card, since this was the closest thing they had.

The card for me was a non-starter because it had foreign transaction fees. To get the 2.5, 3 or 4% you needed to tie up 5k, 50k or 100k in a USBANK savings account. The people who had the $$$ to do this would most likely never carry a balance on the card meaning this was just a giveaway to people with means. Doesn’t make make much sense for a credit card with no annual fee. They should have kept it 2.5% everywhere with at least 5K in savings and no foreign transaction fee. It would have then been somewhat compelling.
